# Invariants (C-D)

<!-- generated by scripts/verify_docs.py --write-nav; do not hand-edit -->

> Code is the source of truth. This file is a map; when it and the code disagree, the code wins.

Every invariant is defined in exactly one file and referenced by id elsewhere.

The index is sharded by family letter: see also [`doctrine/invariants.md`](invariants.md), [`doctrine/invariants-e.md`](invariants-e.md), [`doctrine/invariants-f-m.md`](invariants-f-m.md), [`doctrine/invariants-n-pk.md`](invariants-n-pk.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pl-pq.md`](invariants-pl-pq.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pr-r.md`](invariants-pr-r.md), [`doctrine/invariants-s.md`](invariants-s.md), [`doctrine/invariants-t-z.md`](invariants-t-z.md).

| Id | Statement | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `INV-CB-001` | The callback route serves only names present in the consented overlay; a request for any other name performs no spool mutation. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-002` | A pending state is consumed at most once — the claim-by-rename is the consumption point — and a replayed redirect never rewrites or duplicates a result. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CB-003` | A callback ack binds `(plugin, effective, declaration_digest)`; the ack store fails closed whole-store on any malformed or key-mismatched record; and plugin removal revokes its acks and unroutes. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-004` | Casa relays the query opaquely — the raw query string plus an ordered list of decoded key/value pairs — and interprets only `state`; no provider-specific parsing lives in core. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-005` | For a syntactically-accepted GET that reaches the app, success and every refusal cause yield the same status, headers and redirect target, at any traffic level — there is no throttle response. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-006` | The callback query string never reaches the app access logger, the app handler and exception logs, or the in-container nginx access logs; an unrouted name logs a fixed sentinel. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-007` | Every minted state a casa pass observes ends in exactly one of two ways — a consumer ack, or one terminal outcome written durably before the flow's last credential-bearing artifact is deleted and retained until that ack or the attempt retention bound. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CB-008` | The delivery nudge re-fires on a durable schedule until receipt — the attempt leaving `result_ready` — or until the budget of six accepted dispatches is spent, whichever comes first, and a spent budget raises exactly one operator note. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CB-009` | The consumer's `meta` is size-capped, stored and echoed value-preserving, never interpreted, and never reaches a log surface. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CB-010` | A callback reconcile whose caller is cancelled holds the reconcile lock until the marker and ack writes it has already handed to a worker thread have settled, however many cancellations arrive; and a pass that had already published its overlay delivers one setup-worker kick after those writes settle and before the cancellation propagates. | [`architecture/callbacks.md`](../architecture/callbacks.md) |
| `INV-CB-011` | An operator note the worker attempts while the Telegram channel is not ready, before the channels have finished starting, is logged at INFO without a traceback, and an owed exhaustion or removal note stays owed; every other failed note keeps an ERROR with its traceback. | [`architecture/callback-delivery.md`](../architecture/callback-delivery.md) |
| `INV-CFG-001` | Exactly seven reload scopes exist, and none of them rereads the app manifest options. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-002` | A full reload excludes every other dispatched reload for its duration. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-003` | A live resident identity change is restart-only: an in-process reload neither hot-swaps the resident nor promotes its staged binding on disk before the restart that activates it. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-004` | Only an explicit whitelist of the config tree is version-controlled. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-005` | Reconciliation of the config tree is never boot-fatal. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-006` | In a file reconciled per entry, an entry whose name the image has never shipped is preserved, except when the image ships that name for the first time. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-007` | Reconciliation never writes a config file that fails its schema. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-008` | Entry-level reconciliation only ever writes a `schema_version` that already appears among its input documents; it never synthesizes or migrates one. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-009` | A `${VAR}` placeholder is resolved once its scalar is being built, so a variable's contents are never lexed as part of the document, and a quoted placeholder's value reaches its field unaltered. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-010` | An in-process rewrite of a config file re-emits a scalar the source declared as text and whose whole value is a `${VAR}` placeholder still declared as text, so the rewrite changes neither what that scalar means nor whether the refusal above applies to the file afterwards. | [`architecture/config-reconciliation.md`](../architecture/config-reconciliation.md) |
| `INV-CFG-011` | A reload scope whose handler takes the plugin-mutation lock acquires that lock at the entry point, before the reload read/write lock — never underneath it. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-012` | A reload that reads a specialist's `enabled: false` constructs and registers nothing for it and retires none of its Casa-minted secret slots; and for each of — its runtime agent, its bus queue, its scheduled jobs and webhook routes, its agent-registry entry, its delegation-map entry — the reload either removes it or names the step that failed in its report or its error; whichever scope read the file. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-013` | A specialist read as disabled — by the reload scope that retires it, by an `agents` sweep whether or not it has a runtime Agent, or at boot after the channels start and before background jobs resume — has a close attempted through the terminal funnel, as a named retirement step, for each of its open conversations; a close that fails leaves that conversation open, is told to the operator, is named in the reload's report (at boot, in the log) and is retried by the next `agents` sweep that still reads the specialist disabled; a specialist that failed to load has nothing closed. | [`architecture/configuration.md`](../architecture/configuration.md) |
| `INV-CFG-014` | A configurator run, from any origin, takes the one process-wide configurator lease before its ceiling clock starts and before anything of the run starts, waiting up to `LEASE_WAIT_S` in all, for its lane and then for the holder, for running plugin erasures and for specialist-bundle transactions still running after their handler was cancelled; a run that cannot take it by then is refused with the busy text naming the holder's task and nothing of it runs; the lease is released when the run ends, and a failure before the run starts releases it at once. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-015` | A configurator run that ends while Casa is stopping, whether cancelled or returning after it swallowed the cancellation, leaves its lease record on disk; the next boot removes that record and, once the channels are up, tells the operator once which task was interrupted, unless the job registry's restart recovery announces the same delegation; nothing of the run is replayed. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-016` | A `casa_restart_supervised` call inside a delegated run restarts nothing: it records the need and returns `deferred`; after that run's answer Casa posts one Restart now button, spent on its first tap, which asks the Supervisor for the restart, and a button that expires is edited to say so. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-017` | `config_git_commit`, `casa_reload`, `casa_restart_supervised`, `config_trigger_upsert`, `config_trigger_delete` and `casa_reload_triggers` authorise on the executing role — the `execution_role` Casa stamps on a delegated run's origin, else a bound engagement's role, else the origin's role — and refuse every role but the configurator with `not_authorized`. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-018` | While a configurator run holds the lease, the operator DM neither names nor marks the plugin-health rows whose reason is an install phase (consent pending, a setup-provided value unwired, setup pending, not loaded yet, target pending) of the plugins that run is installing, nor those whose reason is a missing setting (which the run usually wires); every other row is sent as before; and when the lease is released in this process after such a run, a notify pass runs that can name those rows. | [`architecture/configurator.md`](../architecture/configurator.md) |
| `INV-CFG-019` | The configurator commits exactly the values frozen in the approval record the card asks about — the effective settings, the ones kept from the current install included — and an approval that a newer request superseded, or that is no longer its component's current record, writes nothing. | [`architecture/configurator-approvals.md`](../architecture/configurator-approvals.md) |
| `INV-CFG-020` | A run Casa starts for an approval starts only while that approval is approved and its component's current record; the approval is used only by a governed call of that run, of the call's own kind and identity, immediately before its first library call and whatever follows, and every later call under it is refused. | [`architecture/configurator-approvals.md`](../architecture/configurator-approvals.md) |
| `INV-CONC-001` | The bus dequeues per role in priority order and spawns one task per message; it never serializes handler execution. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-CONC-002` | A role has at most one live consumer task, and re-registration replaces the handler while preserving the queue. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-CONC-003` | Turns sharing a session key serialize under the pool entry's lock, decision through publication; distinct keys are concurrent. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-CONC-004` | Every turn serializes under one per-session-key write gate, held from the resume decision through the session-id publish, regardless of which turn path it takes. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-CONC-006` | The graceful stop's completion record carries the number of turns the bus had dispatched and had not finished at the instant it was written, together with the reason they were left — that they are neither awaited nor cancelled — and exactly one record in a stop carries that count. | [`architecture/concurrency-model.md`](../architecture/concurrency-model.md) |
| `INV-DESK-004` | A Telegram DM text message that replies to another message and does not go into a live task reaches the chat's own agent with its text unchanged and one Casa-composed note on the reserved `_reply_note` context key, naming who posted the quoted message — decided from Telegram's sender ids and the task indexes, never from text — when, and what it read, clipped to 600 characters. | [`architecture/telegram.md`](../architecture/telegram.md) |
| `INV-DESK-006` | Each executing agent has one lane and one fault, keyed by the agent alone: every use of it — a stored-call tap, a continuation, a delegation from any chat or bot — waits in one queue of at most three behind one lock, and a faulted agent refuses every use at once until Casa restarts. | [`architecture/agent-lane.md`](../architecture/agent-lane.md) |
| `INV-DOC-001` | Every document repeats the code-wins line verbatim at the top, under front matter carrying `last_reviewed`. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-002` | An architecture document follows one section order — Scope, Mental model, Contracts & invariants, Failure behavior, Extension points, Source & test map — so an agent can skim positionally; documents in the other directories keep the code-wins line and the source map but shape their own sections. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-003` | A document describes the present system — no changelog voice, no "as of version X", no discrepancy log, no TODOs, no open questions; past tense may explain a mechanism, never track the document's own history. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-004` | A cross-cutting rule is defined exactly once, as `**INV-AREA-NNN**: <single-line statement>`, and referenced by id rather than restated. Issue ids sparingly — an id per local rule is bureaucracy, and the define-once check makes over-issuing visibly expensive; nothing mechanical enforces a minimum reference count. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-005` | Anchors are typed symbols (`path/to/file.py::Class.method`, `config.yaml::schema.key`, `tests/test_x.py::test_name`) or tracked bare paths; never `file:line`, which rots silently on the next edit. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-007` | Growth splits, it never appends: the change that crosses the size ceiling lands visibly, the next change touching the over-ceiling document — its file or its manifest row — must split it first, a new path may not be born over the ceiling, and the ceiling is not raised; nothing shards on its own. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-008` | A `Docs-impact:` waiver is checked against the diff it ships with — the waived documents are exactly the documents the change impacts and does not update, no document is waived twice, the reserved token `none` asserts that set is empty, only the tip commit may carry a waiver line, a subject line is never one, and every tip carries a line; whether a waiver's reason is true remains a review question. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-009` | An invariant id cited in a comment or a docstring of a tracked Python file outside `docs/`, in a family the corpus defines, must be an id the corpus defines. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
| `INV-DOC-010` | Generated navigation is rendered only from a manifest that loads — when the root manifest or any `manifest.d/` shard fails to load, the corpus check and `--write-nav` report the source and the error, write no generated artifact, and do not report the navigation as stale. | [`contributing/doc-contract.md`](../contributing/doc-contract.md) |
